note: Hume explains what the customary transition contributes by observing that without it we could not adjust means to ends based on experience. Applying that argument requires the formal trigger and expectation to track the relevant transitions, without turning a necessary condition for adjustment into sufficient practical entitlement. The passage explains why some customary transitions are indispensable; it does not give a reason that the transition occurs in every repeated, triggered case, which the target's universal form requires. That reason remains the missing bridge.
